assumptions: Batch mr_a covers weather only (no venues, no prices), so there are no BOOKING CHECKLIST lines.

Batch mr_b, fast mode: weather and season facts only for New Zealand, Fiji, Bali, Seychelles, Hawaii and Mauritius. No venues, prices, legal steps or real weddings. Reused facts keep their original claim, source, source_type and checked date; only the fact_id changed and a [Copied from ...] note was added where none existed.
Single-month 2026 summaries (New Zealand, Fiji) are single-year observations, not normals, and must be written that way.

Merged by orchestrator from mr_a and mr_b. Single-year observations (NZ and Fiji March 2026) are never presented as typical; base periods and rain-day definitions differ, so places are not ranked by figures.

facts.claim: [Lake Como, nearest official station: Milan] WMO World Weather Information Service, Milan (MILANO), supplied by the Italian Air Force Department of Meteorology, climatological normals for the 30-year period 1971-2000: March mean daily minimum 3.8 C, mean daily maximum 14.3 C, mean total rainfall 65.0 mm, mean number of rain days 6.7. The page does not define a rain day for this station; it carries only the general remark that the averaging period and rain-day definition may differ between countries. Milan is a city station, not on Lake Como.

[Amalfi Coast, nearest official station: Naples] WMO World Weather Information Service, Naples (NAPOLI), supplied by the Italian Air Force Department of Meteorology, normals for 1971-2000: March mean daily minimum 6.3 C, mean daily maximum 15.7 C, mean total rainfall 77.9 mm, mean number of rain days 8.6. No station-specific rain-day definition is stated (general remark only). Naples is a city station, not on the Amalfi Coast itself.

[France: Riviera, Nice] WMO World Weather Information Service, Nice, supplied by Meteo-France, normals for 1971-2000: March mean daily minimum 7.6 C, mean daily maximum 14.9 C, mean total precipitation 60.9 mm, mean number of precipitation days 5.2. Page remarks: 'Mean number of precipitation days = Mean number of days with at least 1 mm of precipitation.' 'Precipitation includes both rain and snow.'

[Portugal: Lisbon] WMO World Weather Information Service, Lisboa, supplied by the Instituto Portugues do Mar e da Atmosfera (IPMA), normals for the 30-year period 1961-1990: March mean daily minimum 9.9 C, mean daily maximum 17.6 C, mean total rainfall 68.9 mm, mean number of rain days 13.0. Page remark: 'Mean number of rain days = Mean number of days with at least 0.1 mm of rain.'

[Mauritius: Port Louis] WMO World Weather Information Service, Port Louis, supplied by Mauritius Meteorological Services, normals for 1971-2000: March mean daily minimum 23.8 C, mean daily maximum 31.5 C, mean total precipitation 83.0 mm, mean number of precipitation days 8.0. Page remark: 'Mean number of precipitation days = Mean number of days with at least 1 mm of precipitation.' (Comparison on the same page: February 160.0 mm and 10.0 days; April 87.0 mm and 7.0 days.)

[Dominican Republic: Punta Cana] WMO World Weather Information Service, Punta Cana, supplied by the Oficina Nacional de Meteorologia (ONAMET), normals for the 30-year period 1961-1990: March mean daily minimum 22.0 C, mean daily maximum 28.1 C, mean total rainfall 54.2 mm, mean number of rain days 6.7. Page remark: 'Mean number of rain days = Mean number of days with at least 1 mm of rain.'

Every WMO World Weather Information Service city page checked in this batch (Milan, Naples, Nice, Lisbon, Port Louis, Punta Cana) carries the remark that the averaging period and the definition of 'Mean Number of Rain Days' (or Precipitation Days) 'may be different for different countries. Hence, care should be taken when city climatologies are compared.' Base periods differ in this batch: 1971-2000 for Milan, Naples, Nice and Port Louis; 1961-1990 for Lisbon and Punta Cana. Rain-day thresholds differ: at least 1 mm (Nice, Port Louis, Punta Cana), at least 0.1 mm (Lisbon), not stated (Milan, Naples).

[Greece: Cyclades, HNMS Naxos station] Hellenic National Meteorological Service climatic data for Naxos (lon 25.369, lat 37.081, altitude 3 m; the page states 'Data Period: None'): March minimum monthly temperature 10.4 C, monthly mean temperature 13.4 C, maximum monthly temperature 15.8 C, monthly mean precipitation height 45.7 mm, monthly mean precipitation days 9.5, monthly mean humidity 71.7%, prevailing wind direction N, monthly mean wind power 14.7 (units on the chart axis: Kt). Naxos is not Mykonos or Santorini; it is the HNMS station used on the August page.

[Switzerland] MeteoSwiss, annual cycle page: 'On the northern side of the Alps, the largest amounts of precipitation normally fall in the summer months, whereas on the southern side of the Alps, the peaks in precipitation tend to occur in spring and autumn.' The same page compares against the normal period 1991-2020. It gives no March-specific figures.

[Switzerland] MeteoSwiss, The climate of Switzerland: 'From late autumn through to spring, low-lying fog regularly forms, predominantly in high pressure areas. This tends to occur mostly along rivers and lakes as the air above these is very damp.' Also: the southern foehn 'occurs primarily between autumn and spring'. 'The coldest temperatures are recorded in January and February.' The page states 'Switzerland has four distinct seasons' and uses the period 1991-2020. No March-specific figures were found on the part of the page read (response truncated after the Snow section began).

[New Zealand, a single year, not a normal] Earth Sciences New Zealand (formerly NIWA), 'Climate Summary for March 2026' (published 8 April 2026, read live 25 November 2026), headline: 'A dry start to autumn for much of New Zealand'. 'March was a mild and mostly settled month for Aotearoa New Zealand, with one significant rain event in the upper North Island, brought on by a tropical low pressure system during the final week of the month.' Rainfall was below or well below normal for Central Otago, the Canterbury High Country, most of Westland, the Marlborough Sounds, most of Wellington, Manawatū-Whanganui, Hawke's Bay, Taranaki and most of Waikato, and above or well above normal for Northland, western Auckland, coastal Bay of Plenty, the Coromandel, western Tasman, North Canterbury and part of Southland. Highest temperature 30.9°C at Alexandra on 7 March; lowest -2.6°C at Pūkaki Airport on 3 March.
facts.conflicts: The March 2026 page states 'The nationwide average temperature in March 2025 was 15.8°C. This is right at the 1991-2020 March average.' The year reads 2025 on a 2026 summary, so the 15.8°C figure is not used until checked against the linked PDF.

facts.claim: [New Zealand, a single year] Earth Sciences New Zealand, Climate Summary for March 2026 (read live 25 November 2026): 'On 25–26 March, a deep subtropical low caused heavy rain, wind, and flooding across much of the country. A red warning for heavy rain was declared for Northland. From Northland to the Bay of Plenty, states of emergency, mass evacuations, power outages, emergency rescues and widespread road closures occurred.' Highest 1-day rainfall was 214 mm at Cathedral Cove on 26 March.

[Copied from get-married-in-new-zealand 03-source-pack fact_115, same source and date.] As at November 2026, Smartraveller New Zealand (updated 22 July 2026, still current at 17 November 2026, read live 17 November 2026): weather conditions can change quickly and severe weather can leave you stranded, especially in remote areas; monitor MetService forecasts and warnings. On the roads, ice, snow, fog, high winds and roaming animals cause hazards, heavy rain can cause landslides, there are few motorways outside major cities, and mountain and ski-field roads can be narrow, unpaved, without barriers and may need snow chains or a 4WD.

[Fiji, a single year, not a normal] Fiji Meteorological Service, Fiji Climate Summary March 2026 (PDF, read live 25 November 2026, extracted text): 'Variable rainfall was recorded during March, with rainfall ranging from well below average to above average. Although it was the Wet Season, the majority of the stations received suppressed rainfall, particularly in the Central and Eastern Divisions.' Of 26 reporting rainfall stations, 5 were above average, 6 average, 13 below average and 2 well below average; the month's highest rainfall was 640.3 mm at Rarawai Mill (Ba).

As at November 2026, Smartraveller Fiji (updated 19 October 2026, still current at 24 November 2026, read live 25 November 2026): 'November to April is cyclone season, but cyclones may occur at other times.' A tropical cyclone's direction and strength can change quickly; during and after a cyclone flights to and from affected areas can be delayed or suspended and available flights may fill quickly. For cyclone updates check the Fiji Meteorological Service.

As at November 2026, Smartraveller Fiji (updated 19 October 2026, read live 25 November 2026): 'Flooding is common, especially in downtown Nadi and on the Coral Coast.' Floods can cut off road access, including access to the airport; monitor road closures on the Fiji Roads Authority Facebook page.

[Copied from bali-wedding-venues 03-source-pack, same source and date.] Smartraveller Indonesia: weather can change quickly during the wet season (usually around October to April; it can differ in Eastern Indonesia). Heavy rains can cause significant flooding in urban areas including Bali, disrupting roads and transport. No temperature or rainfall figures are given.

[Copied from best-time-to-get-married-in-bali 03-source-pack fact_02, same source and date.] Stasiun Klimatologi Bali, Buletin Iklim Bali, May 2024 edition (definitions page): 'Normal monthly rainfall' is the average rainfall for each month over a 30-year period; 'average monthly rainfall' uses a minimum 10-year period. Bali's monthly analysis and forecasts use rain-gauge posts across 20 season zones (Zona Musim, ZOM), the zoning set in 2021. A ZOM is an area whose average rainfall pattern shows a clear difference between the dry-season period and the rainy-season period; areas without that clear difference are 'non-ZOM'.

[Seychelles: Victoria, Mahé] The WMO World Weather Information Service page for Victoria, supplied by the Seychelles Meteorological Authority (read live 25 November 2026), gives March mean daily minimum 25.3°C, mean daily maximum 31.2°C, mean total rainfall 201.9 mm and mean number of rain days 15.0. Remarks: climatological information is based on monthly averages for the 30-year period 1981-2010; a rain day is a day with at least 0.1 mm of rain. For comparison on the same page, January is the wettest month listed (403.7 mm, 20.0 rain days) and July the driest (89.1 mm).

[Copied from getting-married-in-seychelles 03-source-pack fact_117, same source and date.] As at November 2026, Smartraveller Seychelles (updated 28 October 2026, still current at 17 November 2026, read live 17 November 2026): heavy rain can occur, especially during the monsoon season from November to March, causing flooding and landslides that damage roads and infrastructure; if travelling in the wet season, check with operators whether services are affected. Smartraveller links to the Seychelles Meteorological Authority (meteo.sc).

[Copied from getting-married-in-hawaii 03-source-pack fact_118, same source and date.] National Weather Service Honolulu, 'Climate of Hawaiʻi' (statewide, read live 16 November 2026): Hawaii's warmest months are August and September and its coolest are February and March. Winter is the season of more frequent clouds and rainstorms, and the heaviest rains come from winter storms between October and April. Windward coasts and slopes get much more cloud and rain, while leeward areas tend to be sunny and dry, with summers usually dry.

[Copied from mauritius-wedding 03-source-pack fact_111, same source and date.] Smartraveller Mauritius (read live 17 November 2026): cyclone season in Mauritius is from November to May, but cyclones can occur throughout the year, bringing gale force winds, heavy rain, floods and disruption to power and water. During cyclones the airport may close and flights may be cancelled or delayed, so check travel insurance covers this.

[Copied from mauritius-wedding 03-source-pack fact_116, same source and date.] Mauritius Meteorological Services, 'Climate of Mauritius' (read live 17 November 2026): Mauritius has a mild tropical maritime climate with two seasons, a warm humid summer from November to April and a relatively cool dry winter from June to September; October and May are transition months. Mean summer temperature is 24.7 degrees Celsius and mean winter temperature 20.4 degrees Celsius (island-wide, not station-labelled).

[Copied from mauritius-wedding 03-source-pack fact_118, same source and date.] Mauritius Meteorological Services (read live 17 November 2026): long-term mean annual rainfall (1971 to 2000) is 2010 mm; the wettest months are February and March and the driest is October; about 67% of annual rainfall falls in summer, though there is no marked rainy season.

The WMO World Weather Information Service Victoria (Seychelles) page carries the remark: 'Please note that the averaging period for climatological information and the definition of "Mean Number of Rain Days" quoted in this web site may be different for different countries. Hence, care should be taken when city climatologies are compared.'

insider_details.detail: Rain-day counts in this batch use different definitions: Lisbon counts any day with 0.1 mm or more, so its 13 March rain days are not directly comparable with Nice's 5.2 days counted at 1 mm. Quote each station with its own definition, and keep a covered or wet-weather option in every March plan.

For Lake Como and the Amalfi Coast the nearest official March figures are city stations (Milan mean daily max 14.3 C, Naples 15.7 C). Evening receptions at these temperatures need heating, wraps or an indoor fallback in the booking checklist, and the copy must say the figures are from the city station.

Port Louis in March averages 83.0 mm over 8 precipitation days with a mean daily max of 31.5 C, about half February's 160.0 mm. Plan shade, hydration and a rain plan, and describe March only in the source's figures, never as a 'best time'.
On Naxos the HNMS March row shows 9.5 mean precipitation days and a northerly prevailing wind. For island ceremonies that means a wind-sheltered site and a sea-crossing contingency for guests.

Punta Cana's March row (54.2 mm, 6.7 rain days, mean daily max 28.1 C, 1961-1990) is among the drier months on its own WMO table, but the article should state the numbers and leave the comparison to the reader.

Fiji in March sits inside both the met service's wet season and Smartraveller's November to April cyclone season, and flooding is common in downtown Nadi and on the Coral Coast, so build a buffer day before the ceremony and confirm the venue's wet-weather and evacuation plans in writing.

March 2026 in New Zealand was mostly settled but ended with a subtropical low that closed roads from Northland to the Bay of Plenty, so for North Island autumn weddings keep transfer routes flexible and watch MetService warnings in the final week.

Victoria on Mahé averages about 202 mm of rain over 15 rain days in March on the official 1981-2010 normals, and Smartraveller flags heavy rain in the November to March monsoon season, so plan an undercover option and check sea conditions for any inter-island boat transfers.
In Hawaii the heaviest rains come from winter storms between October and April and fall mostly on windward coasts, so for a March wedding ask whether the venue is on the leeward or windward side.

Mauritius Meteorological Services lists February and March as the wettest months, and Smartraveller puts cyclone season from November to May, so check that travel insurance covers cyclone disruption to flights.
